raw:
{
  "question_intent": "Assessing bank earnings-call responses",
  "main_topics": ["Banking wallet assumptions", "US cards business resilience", "Client readiness", "Business growth and capital allocation"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "So the first question on the banking wallet, a bit of a follow up from Alvaro's earlier question. I guess we should continue to think about the wallet assumptions, -10% for this year, +5% for next year, 2026 being lower than 2024, as more sort of prudent planning scenarios and assumptions rather than a forecast. But what is your best sense of what will actually happen? Or how would you assess client readiness to transact, given the backdrop this morning is different to the backdrop two weeks ago? Secondly on US cards, I appreciate the comments on the resilience of the business through April, in line with the industry more broadly. But I guess in the last few weeks you must have done quite a lot of fire drills around potential macro scenarios, potential adverse outcomes. Has any of that work changed at all how you think about where you want to grow the business or how you want to put more capital to work? Thank you.",
  "answer_quote": "Thanks, Chris. So, the way you characterise Banking is the way you should characterise how we approach business in general, which is that we will plan on, I would say, a reasonable basis and the $80 billion for the current year is roughly the 10 year average, well actually $84 billion is the decade average. So it's nothing more than that, it's not scientific, we just think it's a reasonable number for which we should plan. In doing so, we're trying to put some operational tension into the businesses, because clearly I want them to reach the returns goals and by doing so, that must be on the basis of a blend of market share gain consistently delivered, prudent management of risk and driving the efficiency and effectiveness of the business. It cannot be on the basis of a heroic or high market assumption, so that's why we do that. But it is a prudent assumption, [and] you should expect us to monetize at any environment around us and that's why we've invested in the business. Again, expect us to be ready as and when the market picks up. It feels like that readiness to transact, if you like, won't be universal because different sectors are clearly getting clarity at different stages of time. Different geographies are getting clarity at different stages of time. So if you're running either a US corporate or a large global corporate, it actually depends on the specifics of your business model, and we hear that very strongly as we talk to clients. So I think it feels unlikely that we'll wake up tomorrow and the world will have gone back to wherever we thought it was in Davos. But as clarity emerges in different geographies and sectors, hopefully we'll see some coming back, but in the meantime, we continue to drive operational effectiveness. In terms of US cards, this is a business that we've run for 20 years, so it's not new to us. This environment is not new to us. Therefore, what have we done over the last few weeks? The answer is nothing significantly more than we would do ordinarily in this business, because that's just the way we run it, that's the way we understand it. So as you can imagine, even back in 2023, we were cutting unused credit lines, because we knew that unemployment was bound to rise in the US because it was at such low levels. We've been extremely cautious about the lower FICOs. You can see that around 13 percent or less, is less than 660. And actually, if you look at [slide] 38, you'll see that the flow into those lower FICOs is lower than the stock. So that tells you that the credit risk decisions that we're making on the margins are very thoughtful. We are fully staffed in our collections capability and we're really thoughtful about that. So when we see a change in consensus, as we saw in 2023 and 2024 for US unemployment, we don't just change our IFRS9 result, we actually deploy the business to do something different. So whether that's the way we interact with customers, or the fact that we might be putting more people into that collection capability. So we're ready, but the business is very calm and very confident because we've weathered this kind of environment before. We're also very focused on these other [areas], which is deploying the deposit strategy, deploying the efficiency strategy, because from their perspective the most effective thing they can do is improve the returns of business.",
  "reason": "The response provides a direct answer to the earnings-call question, with high evidence level due to the inclusion of specific figures ($80 billion and $84 billion), and narrative alignment as it directly addresses the topics of banking wallet assumptions, US cards business resilience, client readiness, and business growth and capital allocation."
}
